status: Session draft for gate GSP07 (SP07 stale tracker cache, background refresh); NOT registered, no measured run. Registration copies the plan and rule into gsp07-v1-plan.json / gsp07-v1-protocol.json with source manifest and script hashes, after a non-measurement wiring smoke on the candidate image. Open questions below must be settled first.
item: SP07: C0 = legacy (indexer_cache_hard_ttl_seconds 0 = today's cache; breaker off, Tech Info prefetch off) vs C7 = swr (hard TTL 86400 s = 24 h, the user's UX/SLO decision, row 5; indexer_cache_refresh_max_in_flight 4; breaker off, prefetch off). The soft TTL is the product's 1800 s, shortened in-process by the harness (--imdb-cache-ttl).
runner: scripts/run_sp_search_gate.py unchanged: one fresh --network none container per run (cpuset 0,1, 2 CPU, 1 GiB); per repetition the variant order and the arm order rotate; repetition r uses --seed 20261112 + r for both arms; 2 series x 5 repetitions x 3 variants x 2 arms = 60 runs.
time_note: Time scale 1 (the product's 1.5 s Tech Info budget is an unscaled code constant). 24 cold requests every 6 s, each with an immediate warm pair; the stale request for cold i is due 30 s after it (soft TTL 20 s, so the entry is soft-expired), then a followup once the background refreshes settled. Last stale event at ~168 s: ~3 min per run with container start, ~3 h in total.

harness_semantics.stale: same IMDb id (ep: S01E02) S seconds after the cold request, stream response cache invalidated; tracker IMDb cache entry soft-expired (age >= --imdb-cache-ttl), far below the hard TTL
harness_semantics.followup: same request again after every SP07 background refresh settled (C0 has none)
harness_semantics.tracker_calls: synthetic tracker searches from the request start until its background refreshes settled
harness_semantics.new_upload_visible: mu: a stream of the extra '-new' release is in the response; ep: an S01E02 stream is in the response
harness_semantics.variants: m = static trackers; mu = every tracker lists one more release of the movie after the warm request; ep = series requests, trackers list 4 S01E01 releases each, one S01E02 release each appears after the warm request, stale/followup ask S01E02

why_seed_per_rep: As in GSP06: both arms of a repetition see the same per-tracker jitter sequence (the background refresh of C7 takes the draw that the synchronous refresh of C0 takes, in the same order), repetitions sample different sequences.

expected_mechanism.m: C0: the soft-expired entry is dropped, the stale request waits a full tracker search (~0.4 s + jitter); C7: the old list at once (~warm path), one background refresh per tracker. Same tracker calls (3 per stale request), identical sources in every row.
expected_mechanism.mu: C0: the stale request refetches, sees the new release and downloads its .torrent; C7: the old list at once (no new release, by design), the refresh lands it, the followup shows it and downloads it. Stale rows differ by design; followup rows must show the new release in both arms.
expected_mechanism.ep: C0: synchronous refetch finds S01E02. C7: the old list has 0 playable streams for S01E02, so find_by_imdb asks a forced (allow_stale=False) refresh before the name fallback; it joins the background refresh started by the same request, so still 3 tracker calls. Identical sources; latency about the same (one extra DB/resolve pass in C7).

wiring_smoke: Not a measurement (worktree code, in-process, no Docker; --smoke --scenarios S1 --requests 3 --interval 2 --time-scale 0.2 --imdb-cache-ttl 3 --stale-after 4 --steady-from 0, legacy vs swr; n = 3, ms in unscaled units): m stale p50 568 -> 41 ms (warm 42/43), stale tracker calls 3/3, total calls 18/18; mu stale p50 669 -> 45 ms, new release visible stale 1.0 -> 0.0, followup 1.0/1.0; ep stale p50 778 -> 870 ms, S01E02 visible in every stale and followup row of both arms, stale tracker calls 3/3. 0 external HTTP attempts. Note: mu followup Tech Info enrichment differs between arms (the product enriches the first 5 torrents in source order and the new release lands at a different position), so mu is excluded from enrichment identity.

decision_rule.machine_rule: scripts/decide_sp_search_gate.py (unchanged; the hard checks marked 'needs_decide_extension' below require a new, separately hashed checker at registration)
decision_rule.statistic: per-run steady-window (cold requests 2..23 and their warm/stale/followup rows) latency p50/p95 (ms), mean tracker calls per request and mean new-release visibility; pooled n = 10 runs per arm and variant; difference of means; 10 000 bootstrap resamples, seed 20261113; one-sided p-values; Holm per family at alpha 0.05
needs_decide_extension: ep:S1 every stale and followup row of both arms has new_upload_visible = true (S01E02 found: new-episode protection)
mu:S1 every followup row of both arms has new_upload_visible = true (the background refresh landed)
mu:S1 identical source digests in cold, warm and followup rows (stale rows differ by design)
C7 stale + followup tracker calls per index <= C0's (no refresh storm): per-row, not only the bootstrap mean
pass_if_all: both improvements significant after Holm: m and mu stale steady p50 lower
no guard regression after Holm over the guard family (latency, tracker calls, new-release visibility)
identical per-request source digests in m and ep, and identical rendered streams in m, across all runs of both arms
descriptive_only: ep stale latency p50/p95 (C7 adds the forced refresh step; see open question 2)
mu stale new-release visibility (0 in C7 by design: the accepted SWR staleness, bounded by the next request and the hard TTL)
mu followup latency and Tech Info enrichment

open_questions: 1. Run time vs time scale: ~3 h at time scale 1 (as GSP06); time scale 0.5 would halve it but inflates the unscaled CPU share (synthetic .torrent build) in the reported ms equally for both arms.

2. ep stale latency: guard with a margin (needs per-entry margins in a new decide-script version; the current one only has per-metric guard_margin) or descriptive only (this draft). C7 does one extra DB/resolve pass before joining the refresh.
3. Hard checks in 'needs_decide_extension': a new checker (e.g. decide_sp_search_gate_v2.py) instead of editing decide_sp_search_gate.py, whose hash is registered in gsp06-v1.

4. A subject-down variant (S2) would show the largest C7 gain (stale list instead of a 12.5 s tracker timeout) but drifts the 6 s schedule in C0; left out, the breaker (SP05/b, on by default) already shortens that case.
5. Torznab: the product passes allow_stale=False there (Sonarr/Radarr get no stale list when SP07 is on; identical to today when off). Confirm as product behaviour; not measured by this gate.
